species.real: The orange in ochre-stained water is iron hydroxide, more or less rust, and it settles as a sludge that smothers stream beds and the insects living in them.
species.name: Rustelver

dex.text: Wriggles up the cut from the old tunnel with a coat of rust it is rather proud of. Leaves a little orange cloud behind it wherever it has been.
dex.fact: The water coming out of the Harecastle Tunnel on the Trent and Mersey Canal runs bright orange, stained by iron ochre seeping in from old coal and ironstone workings.

species.real: Red ochre stained the bones of the 'Red Lady of Paviland', a Stone Age burial found in a Gower cave in 1823. The lady turned out to be a young man.
species.name: Ochreel

dex.text: Lies in the dark of a canal tunnel with only its eyes showing, waiting for a boat. Boaters legging it through used to sing to keep their spirits up. It liked that.
dex.fact: James Brindley's first Harecastle Tunnel took eleven years to dig and opened in 1777. Boats had no towpath inside, so the boatmen lay on their backs and walked the boat through along the roof: legging.
